note: LLM-authored team write-ups. Grounded in scripts/build_draft_context.py's computed signals (handcuffs, keeper age/risk, positional need, VOR/ADP/slot_delta, news) plus football knowledge (injury history, player archetypes). Rendered by draft.js in place of the deterministic recap() when present.

teams.ddhk: Carried in Christian McCaffrey, James Cook and CeeDee Lamb — ~724 projected points of blue-chip production. The one crack is McCaffrey at 30 with a long injury history, which is exactly why the round-10 stab at Kaelon Black is smart rather than wasteful — it's insurance on the one pick that would sink this roster if it broke. With the backfield and receiver room already deep, ddhk spent the middle rounds buying ceiling: the MarShawn Lloyd pick at 85 looked like a 32-slot reach until Josh Jacobs' exempt-list stint handed Lloyd the Packers' Week-1 job (~Round 7 value now), and late rookies Emmett Johnson and Zachariah Branch are dart throws on athletic upside, not roster filler. Best straight value: Eddy Pineiro, 19 slots past the board.
teams.danseung: A young, injury-light core — Ja'Marr Chase, Chase Brown and rookie Omarion Hampton (702 pts, none over 26) — means no aging star to handcuff and freedom to chase value. Garrett Wilson anchors the receivers and Quinshon Judkins was a clean value in the 2nd. Drake Maye at pick 3 and a last-round Bo Nix (92 slots past the board) turn quarterback into a cheap two-man rotation rather than a spent early pick. Rookie Omar Cooper is the speculative WR stash. A balanced, high-floor build with the league's cleanest keeper trio.
teams.spiffster: Bijan Robinson and rookie phenom Ashton Jeanty give spiffster two bell-cow backs plus Nico Collins (724). The round-13 Mike Washington pick is a direct handcuff to Jeanty — not an age play, but insurance on a rookie workhorse whose projected volume is a double-edged sword. DJ Moore in the 1st is a mild reach on ADP but a high-floor target hog, and Tank Dell is an IR stash, not a live pick — he opens on injured reserve. Jaxson Dart 26 slots late is the upside QB flier.
teams.andyxia124: Derrick Henry (32), Amon-Ra St. Brown and Brock Bowers headline (668), and Henry is the tell: still elite, but at 32 the age cliff is real — and andyxia drafted no handcuff behind him, the roster's biggest single risk. Lamar Jackson in the 1st doubles down on a high-ceiling, boom build. The receiver room is stacked (Jameson Williams, Brian Thomas) but several mid-round picks went ahead of the board. Dylan Sampson is a late RB dart — arguably where the Henry insurance should have come earlier.
teams.Pkizzle3000: De'Von Achane (currently Questionable) and Saquon Barkley (29) are a high-end but fragile RB base alongside rookie TE Colston Loveland (631). The round-6 Jaylen Wright grab reads as a 71-slot reach on paper, but as the Achane handcuff on an already-dinged lead back it's defensible insurance, not a blunder. Emeka Egbuka and Rome Odunze are the receiver bets up top, and Jalen Hurts adds a rushing-QB floor. Rookies Chris Bell and Fernando Mendoza are pure end-of-bench lottery tickets.
teams.sallyyoon84: The thinnest keeper haul in the league — Justin Jefferson, Kyren Williams and rookie Tyler Warren (557) — meant sallyyoon had to draft for production, and George Pickens (68 VOR) was a genuine coup. Blake Corum is the sensible Kyren Williams handcuff given the Rams' committee tendencies. Two-way rookie Travis Hunter in the 13th is the highest-ceiling dart on any bench, and Brock Purdy 76 slots late makes QB an afterthought. Aggressive value hunting to make up for a light head start.
teams.jonsung: An unusual all-RB keeper base — Jonathan Taylor, David Montgomery (29) and Travis Etienne (634) — that's deep at the position but leaned on receivers early, opening with Zay Flowers and D'Andre Swift before landing George Kittle as a value TE. Montgomery's age is a minor flag, but with three startable backs kept there was no need to handcuff. Jayden Daniels is a dual-threat QB value in the 4th. The build is production-now with a thinner ceiling than the contenders above it.
teams.edgxrjiang: Puka Nacua leads, but Ladd McConkey and Bucky Irving are both carrying Questionable tags — an injury cloud over two of three keepers (626). That makes the early Bhayshul Tuten pick and its Chris Rodriguez handcuff a coherent attempt to build a stable backfield behind uncertainty. Tee Higgins is the WR anchor, and Matthew Stafford 68 slots past the board is elite late-QB value. Nicholas Singleton was the clearest reach. A roster that lives or dies on keeper health.
teams.IconicJH: Jahmyr Gibbs, Chris Olave and Trey McBride form a strong, young spine (682). The draft chased running back hard — Kenny Gainwell, Jacory Croskey-Merritt and Rachaad White as a Croskey-Merritt handcuff — a scattershot approach that produced a few reaches. Zach Charbonnet at 97 is confirmed a reach by the news: he's on PUP, out at least four games, with rookie Jadarian Price now in the picture. Elite up top (A.J. Brown, Terry McLaurin), muddier in the RB dart pile.
teams.eikichii952: The league's richest keeper trio by projection — Josh Allen, Kenneth Walker and DeVonta Smith (776) — and it shows in a balanced board with no positional holes and no real reaches. Tetairoa McMillan and Cam Skattebo were early hits, Joe Burrow (17 past board) is luxury QB depth behind Allen, and Travis Kelce is a steady TE. Worth monitoring: Walker's situation has been in flux this offseason. The most complete, lowest-variance roster in the field.
teams.sathwikn: The exempt-list story cuts the other way here: Josh Jacobs is sathwikn's kept RB, and with him now out indefinitely and no handcuff drafted (Lloyd went to ddhk), a keeper cornerstone just evaporated. Drake London (Questionable) adds to the uncertainty (584 base). The draft leaned into rookies — Jeremiyah Love in the 1st, TreVeyon Henderson — and landed the board's best value at the position in Sam LaPorta (17 past board, 32 VOR). Upside is real, but the Jacobs blow makes this the roster most reshaped by news.
teams.Paul_Yoon: An all-receiver keeper base — Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Malik Nabers (Q) and Rashee Rice (Q) — with two carrying Questionable tags, so the draft had to manufacture a backfield, and did: Javonte Williams, Jadarian Price, J.K. Dobbins, Jonathon Brooks and a Jordan Mason/Demond Claiborne handcuff pair. Claiborne at 86 slots ahead of the board is the league's biggest reach on paper, but it's a deliberate lottery ticket on the Mason backfield. Dak Prescott 51 late rounds out a committee-by-design build.
